title: Where everything is
intro: Five minutes that save you weeks of wandering around. This guide shows you what's in each section of the menu, what each one is for, and in what order it makes sense to use them. By the end, you'll know exactly where to look for anything.

theory.title: The training has a backbone: the Program
theory.text: In the left-hand menu, "Program" is the guided path: short lessons, in order, each with tasks you check off as you complete them. It's the path you follow start to finish. Everything else in the menu is support: you look things up, you copy things, you go deeper... but real progress is measured there. The progress bar at the bottom of the menu always tells you how many lessons of the path you've completed.
theory.analogy: The Program is the highway; the other sections are the rest stops: you pull in when you need them, but the trip is the highway.

theory.title: Three libraries to copy from: Prompts, Kits, and Agents
theory.text: "Prompts" is the library of ready-to-copy professional requests, organized by topic and by tool, with [LIKE THIS] blanks you fill in with your own case. "Institutional Kits" are complete end-to-end projects: each kit comes with its brief, its architecture, its step-by-step phases, its prompts, its importable n8n flow, its tests, its legal side, and even how to price it. "Agents" are complete, ready-to-install configurations: Claude Code subagents, custom GPTs, n8n agent flows, and API-based agents with their code, each with step-by-step installation and a test to confirm it works.
theory.analogy: Prompts are stock phrases; a Kit is the full recipe for the dish; an Agent is an appliance you plug in and it works on its own.

theory.title: Tools: the profile page for each app
theory.text: In "Tools" there's a page for each application taught here (ChatGPT, Claude, n8n, Gemini, GitHub, WhatsApp, Telegram...). Each profile explains what pieces the tool has inside, when to use it and when not to, its specific prompts, and — for tools that automate things — its library of automations with steps, credentials, and a test. The lesson counts you see on each profile are calculated automatically from the actual content: if it says 12, there are 12.
theory.analogy: It's the instruction manual for each machine in the workshop, with its recipes right next to it.

theory.title: Automations live in two places, and there's a logic to it
theory.text: The 40 importable n8n workflows live in the n8n profile (Tools → n8n), each with its credentials guide: what to create in Telegram with @BotFather (free), what WhatsApp Business Cloud needs (a Meta account), how to connect Gmail or Google Sheets. And on top of that, each Institutional Kit comes with its own project-specific flow. Easy rule: want a standalone automation? → Tools. Building a full project? → its Kit.

theory.title: The rest of the menu, one line each
theory.text: "Home": where you stand today and your next step. "My project": the questionnaire that turns your goal into recommendations, and where your favorite prompts get saved. "Questions": typical doubts answered briefly. "Dictionary": over 500 AI terms explained in plain English, with links to the lessons where they come up. "Progress": what you've done so far, your exportable notebook, and the delete button. "Guides": this section, with the fundamentals worth reading before anything else. And the "Block library" inside each area of the path: the expanded reference material, hundreds of entries organized by stage.

tasks.title: Find the Program and your next lesson
tasks.action: Open "Program" in the menu. Look at the number of lessons in the path and find the first one you haven't completed. Don't do it now: just check that you know how to get back to it.
tasks.expect: You can say, without looking, which lesson is next and how many you've done.
tasks.stuck: If you don't see the menu, tap the three-line icon in the top left (on mobile the menu is collapsed).

tasks.title: Open a kit and go through its tabs
tasks.action: Go into "Institutional Kits" and pick the one closest to something you'd like to build. Go through its tabs in order: what it is, the brief, the architecture, the phases, the prompts, the importable flow, the tests, the cost, and the delivery.
tasks.expect: You understand that a kit isn't a list of ideas: it's a whole project with everything you need inside.
tasks.stuck: If you're torn between two kits, open the "What it is and who it's for" tab on both and compare the "Not a fit for" list.

tasks.title: Find the automations library
tasks.action: Open "Tools", go into n8n, and scroll down to the automations library. Open one that uses Telegram or WhatsApp and read its credentials section.
tasks.expect: You see the exact credential steps: BotFather for Telegram, Meta Business for WhatsApp. Now you know where all the automations live.
tasks.stuck: If you can't find the n8n profile, use the search (Ctrl K) and type "n8n".

tasks.title: Look at an agent from the inside
tasks.action: Open "Agents", filter by the platform you already use (ChatGPT or Claude Code, for example), and open one. Read its capabilities, its limits, and the ready-to-copy file.
tasks.expect: You see that each agent comes with the full configuration, step-by-step installation, and a test to verify it.
tasks.stuck: If none of the platforms ring a bell, start with a custom GPT: it only needs a ChatGPT account.

tasks.title: Learn the shortcut that finds everything
tasks.action: Press Ctrl K (or Cmd K on Mac), type "invoice", and look at the results: lessons, prompts, and related profiles. Try it with another word from your own work.
tasks.expect: The search returns results from every section at once. It's the shortest path when you don't know where something is.
tasks.stuck: If the shortcut doesn't respond, click the "Search..." box in the side menu: it's the same thing.

tasks.title: Look up a term that sounds like gibberish
tasks.action: Open "Dictionary" and search for a term you've heard and aren't sure about (for example "token", "RAG", or "webhook"). Read the short definition and the analogy.
tasks.expect: Every term has a plain-English explanation and links to the lessons where it's actually used.
tasks.stuck: If the term isn't there, note it down: the search (Ctrl K) usually finds it inside some lesson.

canDo: Find any prompt, kit, agent, automation, or term without wandering around.
Always know your next step: the Program marks it for you.
Use the search (Ctrl K) as a universal shortcut from any screen.
Save prompts and decisions in My project so you don't lose them.
cantDo: Skip the Program and expect the libraries to structure your learning for you: they're support, not the path.
Set up an automation with real data without first going through its credentials guide and its test.
Rely on memory: if something was useful to you, save it in My project or in your notebook.
words: The guided path of lessons in order. Your backbone.
A complete packaged project: brief, phases, prompts, flow, legal, and price.
A ready-to-install AI configuration that works on a specific task with clear limits.
The request you write to an AI. The ones here come with [LIKE THIS] blanks to fill in.
An n8n automation flow: you import it, connect credentials, and test it.
The expanded reference material for each stage of the path.
Your space: it turns your goal into recommendations and saves your prompts.
The search shortcut. Finds lessons, prompts, profiles, and terms all at once.
